Odin × Godot

Pure-Odin events — events.Event(T)

3 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
Choose events or engine signalsModule and subscriber lifetime requirementsHot reloadSemantics reference

Use events.Event(T) for typed notifications between Odin scripts in the same library. import events "godot:events" provides an observer list that invokes subscribers through direct procedure calls, without engine dispatch, Variant boxing, or allocation during emit. Engine signals also perform a StringName lookup, box arguments into Variants, dispatch through Object::emit_signal, and call back into Odin through C. Use those signals when the notification crosses a module or engine boundary.

Odin
import events "godot:events"

Spawner :: struct {
	owner: gd.Node2d,
	slow_changed: events.Event(f64), // untagged field: private, pure Odin
}

// publisher
events.emit(&self.slow_changed, 0.5)

// subscriber (ctx points to the receiving script struct, as in flow callbacks)
events.subscribe(&spawner.slow_changed, self, enemy_on_slow, owner_id)

enemy_on_slow :: proc(ctx: rawptr, factor: f64) {
	self := cast(^Enemy)ctx
	self.slow = f32(factor)
}

The payload can be any Odin type, including a struct, slice, or pointer. It is passed by value and checked at compile time, without the gd.Int/f64 restrictions or Variant marshalling required by engine signals. Normal Odin value-copy and referenced-data lifetime rules still apply.

Choose events or engine signals#

use
Crossing a boundary: another script module, GDScript, .tscn [connection]s, the Inspector, the editor engine signal (gd.Signal1(int) / gd.SignalN(struct{...}) fields): uses the engine's connection mechanism
One-to-many notifications between scripts in the same module/dll events.Event(T): direct calls, typed payloads
Per-bullet or per-frame-per-entity loops batch and iterate when callback overhead matters (see barrage's SOA bullet field)

Module and subscriber lifetime requirements#

1. Same module only. Script modules are isolated dlls with no cross-imports (modules). A subscription is a raw proc pointer plus a struct pointer, and these are not a supported cross-module interface: typeids are module-local, and rt.script_of returns nil for another module's class. When a trigger comes from another module, make one engine call into the module that owns the event, then use Event to notify its subscribers. Barrage's SlowEnemies powerup uses this arrangement: pickup.odin (powerups module) makes one object_call("slow_all_enemies") into the Spawner (enemies module), which events.emits to every subscribed Enemy:

Text
powerups dll                       enemies dll
pickup ── object_call (engine) ──> spawner ── events.emit (direct) ──> enemy
                                                                  ├──> enemy
                                                                  └──> enemy

2. Unsubscribe before the subscriber dies. The subscription stores your struct pointer raw; if the script instance is freed first, the next emit is a use-after-free. For a node script, do it in <class>_exit_tree, which fires on queue_free and on scene teardown:

Odin
enemy_exit_tree :: proc(self: ^Enemy) {
	if sp := find_spawner(self); sp != nil {
		events.unsubscribe_owner(&sp.slow_changed, u64(gd.object_get_instance_id(cast(gd.Object)self.owner)))
	}
}

The publisher frees its list in its own exit_tree with events.destroy.

Hot reload#

Subscriptions store procedure pointers. Before moving a live publisher or subscriber to a new DLL generation, the core requires a reload hook. Without one, it keeps the instance on the old generation and emits a warning. A reload that changes layout also reallocates structs, invalidating old ctx pointers. Resubscribe in <class>_reload, using an owner tag to remove stale subscriptions first. This makes repeated calls safe regardless of the order in which instances are rebound, as with flow's Action trees:

Odin
enemy_subscribe_slow :: proc(self: ^Enemy) {
	sp := find_spawner(self)
	if sp == nil {return}
	id := u64(gd.object_get_instance_id(cast(gd.Object)self.owner))
	events.unsubscribe_owner(&sp.slow_changed, id) // idempotent
	events.subscribe(&sp.slow_changed, self, enemy_on_slow, id)
}

enemy_ready  :: proc(self: ^Enemy) { /* ... */ enemy_subscribe_slow(self) }
enemy_reload :: proc(self: ^Enemy) { enemy_subscribe_slow(self) }

After all affected reload hooks return, the old generation may unload. Each hook must therefore remove or replace subscriptions holding an old fn or ctx pointer before returning.

This applies to //gd:tool scripts and editor-driven reloads. Ordinary game scripts do not hot-reload during a run.

Semantics reference#

  • subscribe(e, ctx, fn, owner = 0) appends the subscription. Duplicates are allowed, and each fires once. owner is a caller-chosen tag (use the engine instance id) for bulk removal.
  • unsubscribe(e, ctx, fn) removes the first (fn, ctx) match.
  • unsubscribe_owner(e, owner) removes every subscription with that tag.
  • emit(e, payload) calls live subscribers in subscription order. It is reentrancy-safe: subscribing during an emit defers to the next emit, and unsubscribing during an emit takes effect immediately (a not-yet-called subscriber removed mid-emit will not fire). Nested emits are supported.
  • count(e) returns the live count, clear(e) drops all subscriptions, and destroy(e) frees the event. destroy must not run from inside one of the event's own callbacks.
  • Not thread-safe. Use events on the main gameplay thread.

The package is engine-agnostic (no godot import) and unit-tested standalone: tests/events/run.sh (suite entry events, sentinel EVENTS_OK).
